questions.question: In your own words, what is the main difference between a graded and an ungraded river profile?
questions.expected_answer: A graded profile is smooth and concave, showing a balance between erosion and deposition. An ungraded profile has irregularities or knickpoints (like waterfalls), showing the river is still actively eroding to reach equilibrium.

questions.question: Explain the two main causes that can lead to a river experiencing rejuvenation.
questions.expected_answer: Rejuvenation happens when a river's permanent base level drops relative to the land. This can occur either because the land mass itself undergoes tectonic uplift, or because there is a global (eustatic) drop in sea level.

questions.question: When looking at a cross-sectional diagram, how can you identify that a river has been rejuvenated?
questions.expected_answer: You will see a steep, deep V-shaped channel (incised meander) cut into an older, wider valley, with stepped flat surfaces on the valley sides known as river terraces, which are the remains of the old flood plain.
